Every planned screenshot uses clear IMAGE PLACEHOLDER text pending UI approval. Product release readiness remains separate. Multiple AEM instances. Separate folders. One desktop experience. Sambafied’s intended advantage is concurrent access to distinct AEM instances through separate work folders in one client. That complete simultaneous workflow is still under development. Named connection and mount primitives exist; they are not proof of end-to-end multi-instance readiness.

Adobe Experience Manager desktop app already supports native desktop work: opening and editing assets, revealing downloaded files or folders, and explicitly uploading local changes. See Adobe’s getting-started guide. Adobe also documents changing the connection to a different server. Its troubleshooting section explains that old cookies can interfere with authentication and prescribes logging out of the current session and clearing cookies before reconnecting in that situation. See Login issues when switching to a different server. That is evidence of a server-switching workflow. It does not establish that cookie clearing is always needed, or provide an explicit current-version statement that only one server/session can ever be connected. We do not turn the absence of documented concurrent mappings into proof that they are impossible.

Adobe’s v3 release notes describe automatic upload of new files under downloaded folders and collection synchronization. The comparison is about Explorer-first repository access and concurrent per-instance mappings, not a claim that Adobe has no sync or automatic upload behavior.

Question Adobe’s documented workflow Sambafied direction and boundary How do I reach assets? Native application open/edit and file/folder reveal actions. A native work folder as the starting point; bounded Windows/local AEM evidence exists. What happens across servers? Connection changes between servers are documented, with logout/cookie-clearing guidance for authentication interference. The reviewed sources do not document concurrent per-instance work-folder mappings. Multiple AEM instances available simultaneously in distinct folders, within one client. Complete concurrent operation still needs qualification. Does saving publish edits? Upload Changes explicitly sends local edits to AEM. Local save and remote publication are distinct. Bounded local adapters exist; production sync acceptance remains open.

For teams working across brands, environments, or repositories, evaluate whether assets from each instance can remain available side by side, whether their destinations are clear, and how independent authentication and publication behave. Sambafied’s multi-instance goal is to reduce connection switching as people move between repositories. It is a product direction, not a released feature or a promise of cross-instance migration. Sambafied is an independent project and is not affiliated with Adobe. No endorsement, feature parity, performance advantage, or certified compatibility is claimed. Sources reviewed 20 October 2026. Observation Next step Another user changed the remote asset Recheck the remote version and review your local changes before publication. Upload returned an uncertain result Inspect the recorded operation and remote result before retrying. Sign-in expired Reauthenticate the intended connection; do not change the destination to get around the failure. AEM as a Cloud Service and local AEM are both in Sambafied DAM Client’s product scope. Use a separate connection and work folder for each environment. The public product is coming soon.

Obtain the Author URL and account access for the intended Cloud Service environment. Do not substitute a delivery URL, a storage URL, or an unrelated Adobe service endpoint. The inspected desktop connection design uses the Author’s own sign-in page. A Cloud Service Author can present Sign in with Adobe and continue through the organization’s identity flow. The desktop validates the resulting Author session before passing it to the agent. The provider hint in the connection UI is not itself proof that an operation is supported.

Record the exact candidate build and Cloud Service Author environment. Confirm the account can access the required DAM subtree. Complete the Author’s sign-in flow in the desktop window. Check the displayed principal and Author. Use a distinct, new empty local work folder and evaluate the explicitly enabled operations. If the candidate requires additional non-secret client configuration, use its matching instructions. Do not borrow another application’s client identity or treat a guessed OAuth registration as a supported integration.

A successful sign-in does not prove search, original download, upload, or processing completion. Cloud Service binary ingestion and on-premises binary writes use distinct adapters and eligibility checks. The source review retains open live Cloud Service and production-operation acceptance gates. This site therefore does not promise all operations for every Cloud Service environment, or infer Cloud readiness from a local Author result. Use readiness and limits to interpret the evidence. Sambafied DAM Client is being built for local AEM and AEM as a Cloud Service. This guide covers the local Author path. The public product is coming soon; these notes describe the inspected development flow.

Have the exact Author URL, an authorized account, a dedicated evaluation DAM subtree, and a new empty work-folder path. Confirm the candidate build’s package identity and Cloud Files preflight before creating a fresh native root. Use HTTPS for normal environments. The development flow permits HTTP only when explicitly configured for a loopback Author; that exception is not a production network configuration.

Enter the Author URL in the desktop connection surface. Select Sign in. The embedded view opens the Author’s own login page. Complete the authentication presented by that Author. Verify the displayed account and Author before choosing the work folder. Select a new empty folder on a qualified local volume. A connection label that already belongs to another Author must not be silently reused. Give separate instances distinct names and destinations. The inspected flow validates the Author session before handing it to the agent. Remembering the connection is an explicit option; it does not replace server-side session checks.

Open the work folder and recall a known test original. Confirm the bytes and the root status. A signed-in account and a populated folder are separate observations: sign-in alone does not prove the folder is connected. Local sign-in, mount, recall, logout, and remembered restore have bounded development evidence. That evidence does not qualify every production on-premises version, SSO profile, proxy, or certificate setup. See getting started for evaluation preparation, the folder workflow for retention, and Cloud Service connections for the other deployment path.

Guide home · Find a task This guide helps users of Adobe Experience Manager desktop app transition to Sambafied. The two applications serve similar purposes but have different architectures, installation methods and workflows.
documents.s: Migrate from Adobe AEM desktop app

documents.t: Complete these steps before installing Sambafied: Back up local work. Export or save copies of any locally edited files that have not been uploaded to AEM. Check the Adobe app's Pending Changes or Modified files view. Note your connections. Record the AEM Author URLs, usernames, and DAM paths you currently use. You will need these to set up Sambafied. Document linked assets. If you have InDesign, Illustrator or Photoshop documents that link to AEM assets, note the current file paths. After migration, you may need to relink these. Clear the Adobe cache (optional). If disk space is a concern, use Adobe's built-in cache cleanup before uninstalling. Do not manually delete files. Uninstall Adobe (optional). You can run both applications side by side during evaluation. Uninstall Adobe only after you have verified Sambafied works for your needs.
See getting started for build instructions. Sambafied is currently a development preview built from source; a production installer is not yet available.

Launch Sambafied. Add a new connection using your AEM Author URL. Sign in when prompted. Choose a work folder location on a local NTFS drive (Windows) or a FUSE-supported path (Linux). See Connections for detailed instructions.
documents.s: Step 2: Set up your first connection

documents.t: Browse to a folder you know exists in AEM. Open a test file to verify download works. Make a small edit and upload to verify write access.

If you have InDesign, Illustrator or Photoshop files that referenced assets through Adobe's desktop app: Open the creative document. The application will report missing links (the old paths no longer exist). Use the application's relink feature to point to the new Sambafied work folder location. Save the document. Important: Adobe's desktop app used paths like \\Server\ShareName\... on Windows. Sambafied uses a different path structure based on the mapped drive or mount point you chose.
Repeat steps 2-4 for each AEM instance you previously connected to.

Adobe automatically creates a folder at a fixed location. Sambafied lets you choose where to store local copies. This gives you more control but requires you to remember where you put things.

Adobe requires separate app instances or profile switching. Sambafied supports named connections, each with its own work folder, making it easier to work with multiple AEM environments simultaneously.

Adobe uses Windows network share paths (\\AdobeServer\...). Sambafied uses drive letters on Windows (S:\...) or mount points on Linux (~/SambafiedMount/...). Creative documents that linked assets through the old paths will need relinking.
Adobe has built-in offline caching. Sambafied's offline support is still under development. Check readiness and limits for current status.
Adobe uses its own credential management. Sambafied uses OS credential storage (Windows Credential Manager or Linux keyring) after browser-based sign-in.
This is expected. Use your creative application's relink feature to update paths.
Check the Adobe cache folder location and back up any needed files before uninstalling.
Both applications work with AEM Assets, but supported file types depend on your AEM configuration, not the desktop app.
Performance depends on many factors: AEM server, network, file sizes and local disk speed. Evaluate with your typical workload.
You can run Adobe AEM desktop app and Sambafied side by side during evaluation. Use different work folder locations to avoid conflicts. Do not connect both to the same AEM folder simultaneously.

Guide home · Find a task Collections group existing DAM assets. They do not create separate editing histories or independent copies. Browsing collections does not imply permission to change their membership. Collections are planned and are not available in the current connected client. Use My assets for current browsing. The following steps describe the intended flow for a future build that provides Collections. Ask your administrator about required server support; do not install additional server components yourself.

These steps are conditional on a future build providing Collections. Live AEM collection behavior has not yet been verified. Open Collections and refresh the list. Open a collection and check whether all members loaded. Browse members and review any download, including subfolders and related files. Inspect individual missing or denied items in Transfers. A collection groups existing assets. An incomplete member list does not mean it is empty. Cancel remaining downloads without deleting completed files. Ask your administrator about collection availability; do not install server components yourself. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Browse and download collections A Sambafied illustration will be added here. No application screenshot is available yet.

The same asset can appear in several collections and My assets. Shared editing behavior is still being checked. Open asset details and check its server location. Inspect local status before editing or downloading another copy. When accessing it through another collection, check that the same local work and checkout state appear. Collection membership does not create a separate asset or editing history. Removing membership differs from deleting the asset. If views disagree, refresh and preserve existing local edits. Do not create another working copy to hide the inconsistency. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Understand collection aliases A Sambafied illustration will be added here. Guide home · Find a task Preserve local edits before resolving conflicts. Compare the local and server copies; timestamps and checkout badges alone do not establish which version should replace the other. Keep recovery files and original connection details after a fault. Recovery should use the account and folder that own the work. Ask support before moving retained state, resetting credentials or discarding files to remove an error.

Be online and close applications writing the file. A current server original and protected recovery copy are required. Select the local edit and choose Discard Changes. Check the asset and the server copy that will replace it. Review the recovery copy and confirmation. Confirm only if this is the saved copy you intend to replace. Discard replaces the reviewed local edit. It does not delete the server asset, upload or check in. Cancel to keep edits. If recovery cannot be secured or the server state is unknown, stop and contact support. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Discard local changes with recovery A Sambafied illustration will be added here. No application screenshot is available yet.

Keep the local file and server information for comparison. Open conflict details. Compare revisions, sizes and timestamps. Use Reveal local or Open in Web if available. Keep an independent copy if unsure. To use the server copy, review local replacement and recovery before confirming. Use Refresh separately for a clean local copy. A lock icon or timestamp alone does not establish which copy should replace the other. Cancel to preserve local work. Resolve an unknown upload result before attempting another overwrite. documents.t: Guide home · Find a task Use Connections to check the server and account before acting. Give each connection a recognizable name. Ask your administrator for the correct Author address and DAM root; do not publish private environment addresses in screenshots or support reports. Sign-in methods depend on the server and build. Remembering the server address differs from remembering sign-in. If a session expires, sign in explicitly for that connection and check the account before resuming pending work.

Have the Author server address, deployment type and DAM root supplied by your administrator. Open Connections and choose the add connection action. Enter a distinct name, deployment type, Author address and DAM root. Connect, then check the displayed account and server. Edit the Explorer display name if needed. Before removing a connection, inspect its pending work. Each connection keeps its own account and work folder. Renaming a display label does not move files. Cancel setup to leave it unfinished. Keep local edits and recovery files if removal reports pending work. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Manage named connections A Sambafied illustration will be added here. No application screenshot is available yet.

The supported sign-in method depends on the server and build. Select the connection and review its sign-in method. Before starting sign-in, choose Remember sign-in if offered and if you want this connection to retain its sign-in securely on this PC. This option is unavailable for the Native sign-in profile. Choose Sign in and complete the page or browser prompt presented by the app. Check the account name after connecting. Remembering the server address and remembering sign-in are separate choices. Cancel while sign-in is pending to abandon the attempt. If access is denied or the browser cannot return to the app, retry from that connection or ask your administrator. Never share sign-in tokens. documents.t: Check which account owns local edits and pending transfers. Open Sign in again when the connection asks you to reconnect. Confirm the original account before resuming pending work. To sign out, choose Log out for that connection. To switch accounts, finish signing out, sign in again and check the new account before starting work. Local edits should survive session expiry and sign-out. Pending work belongs to the account that started it. If a different account appears, leave older pending work untouched and ask support for help. After restart, inspect Transfers before retrying an unknown result. Guide home · Find a task Term Meaning Connection A named server, DAM root, account and work folder. Author server The AEM address supplied for managing assets. Original The full asset file, as distinct from a thumbnail. Work folder The managed Windows location for accessing originals. Cloud-only Visible in the folder, but its original still needs downloading. Available locally The original has downloaded to this PC. Pinned Requested to remain offline; check download progress for completion. Edited locally Saved changes on this PC that may still need uploading. Upload Changes Send a reviewed saved copy to the server. Processing Server work after transfer, which can finish later. Checkout A server reservation or ownership signal; enforcement varies. Check-in Release checkout where supported; separate from upload. Conflict Local and server changes need comparison before replacement. Unknown result The server outcome needs checking before retrying. Collection A group of existing assets, not separate copies. Alias Another view of the same asset, including through a collection. Display title A label, distinct from filename and folder location. Exported copy Independent local data outside the managed upload workflow. Recovery copy Data retained to protect local work during replacement or repair. Saved and effective settings The preference you saved and the value currently applied. Read moving from Adobe desktop app for practical differences.

documents.t: Sambafied AEM Desktop is in development. A public customer installer and supported Windows/AEM version list are not available in this guide. Use only evaluation instructions supplied with your build; Adobe compatibility packages and redistributables are not Sambafied prerequisites.

For a connected build, ask your administrator for the Author address, DAM root, permitted sign-in method and disk requirements. Keep each connection's work folder distinct.

Keep user work, recovery copies, cache and application configuration in place during updates. Changing a display name does not move a work folder. A supported migration procedure is still being prepared. Do not move existing application data into a proposed layout manually.

A supported customer installer and exact installation procedure are not available yet. Obtain an evaluation build and instructions from the responsible product contact. Before updating, inspect pending uploads and back up local edits and recovery data. Follow only the update or rollback instructions supplied for that build. Before uninstalling, review data retention and keep user work by default. An evaluation build is not a supported customer release. Platform compatibility information will accompany a release. documents.t: Have permission to change asset metadata. Choose Change Title. Inspect the current title and enter a new one. Review validation and save. Reopen details to check the result. Changing a title does not rename or move the file. Cancel to keep the title. If permissions or server changes prevent saving, keep the draft and refresh before trying again. Reopen details to check saved values. Check the displayed result after submission. Preserve your draft if the asset changed or access was denied. Use Open in Web if desktop editing is unavailable and your administrator permits it. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Edit metadata A Sambafied illustration will be added here. Have permission to create a folder in the selected parent. Choose Create DAM folder. Enter its name and title; inspect the final name and optional metadata schema. Review and confirm creation. State What it means Cloud-only Download the original while online. Available locally The original is on this PC; cleanup may reclaim eligible clean copies. Pinned or pending Retention was requested; check download completion. Edited locally Saved changes may still need uploading. Queued or uploading Inspect progress for the selected saved copy. Uploaded or processing Transfer and server processing may finish separately. Conflict Compare local and server versions before replacement. Unknown or detached Check the connection, account and result before acting.
If offered, automatic upload requires explicit opt-in for the connection. Check its policy and paused work before relying on it. Saving or pinning alone is not confirmation that a file uploaded.

Download the originals and linked files you need while online. Inspect local availability for each required asset. While offline, open only files whose originals are available on this PC. Save normally. Reconnect to the original connection and account before reviewing uploads. A visible cloud-only file is unavailable offline. Local edits remain separate from uploaded changes. documents.t: Have enough disk space for the selected files and related assets. Select assets or a folder and choose Pin or Keep originals offline, when available. Review files, estimated space and related-file options. Wait for downloads and inspect partial or denied items. Unpin when you no longer need local retention. Pinning requests retention; only completed downloads are available offline. Unpinning does not delete the server asset or local edits. If space is insufficient, reduce the selection. documents.t: Have a Windows application associated with the file type. Select the asset and choose Open. Use Open With to choose another application if offered. Wait for any original download before opening the file. Open uses the local original and does not automatically check the asset out. If no application opens, check the Windows file association and download status. Use Edit when you intend to change the asset. Have edit permission and check whether your server supports checkout. Select the asset and choose Edit. Review any checkout message and download the original if needed. Make changes in your desktop application and save locally. Return to Edited locally, review the saved copy and choose Upload Changes when ready. Saving on this PC does not by itself upload changes. Check-in is separate where supported. If another person changed the server copy or owns checkout, preserve your local file and compare the versions before resolving the conflict. Use the managed work-folder copy for editing and uploading changes. An exported copy is independent of the managed asset. If the destination is unavailable, inspect connection and download status. Do not move or delete cache files to repair it. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Reveal the right folder A Sambafied illustration will be added here. No application screenshot is available yet.

Drag-and-drop is still being checked across Windows and desktop applications. Use Open or Upload File when unavailable. For drag-out, download the original and select the asset. Drag to a supported destination and check whether it creates a copy or link. For drag-in, drop local files on the upload destination offered by the app. Review the target folder, filenames and collision choices before confirming. A drag gesture must not bypass the upload review. Cancel the review to stop an import. If a gesture fails, use the file picker rather than moving files into cache folders. Choose Check in and inspect the result. Treat checkout as advisory in this preview. A badge does not guarantee exclusive editing or replace conflict checking. If another person owns checkout or ownership changes, keep local work and ask your administrator. Upload does not necessarily check in. Read installation and availability. Create a named connection with details from your administrator. Browse or search for a file you can read. Open the original, then use Edit and Upload Changes if you intend to change it. Inspect Transfers for the result.

A preview image is not a downloaded original. Saving in a desktop application does not automatically mean the server copy changed. Upload completion, server processing and check-in can happen separately. Keep local edits until you have checked the result.

Sambafied supports bookmarking frequently used locations. Favorites are stored per profile and generation (the server state when you connected). If a folder moves or renames on the server, the favorite may not resolve.

To reset a preference to its default: Close Sambafied. Delete the corresponding JSON file from the configuration folder. Restart Sambafied. Do not delete profile directories without first backing up any local work.

Preferences vary by build. Some changes need a reconnect or restart. Open Settings or Preferences. Use General for startup/window, Storage for usage/cleanup and Advanced for connection defaults/maintenance. Change values and choose Save. Follow any separate Apply, reconnect or restart instructions. A saved preference may still be waiting to take effect. Keep previous settings if the application fails. documents.t: Cache clear removes eligible local copies. Windows Free up space releases eligible downloaded originals while keeping the server asset visible. Discard Changes replaces a local edit with a server copy and needs recovery protection. Inspect the review before confirming any of them.

When available, review the age in days and exclusions before enabling cleanup. The planned policy uses modified-date age. Check that the setting applied; a quota does not justify removing unuploaded work.

Review eligible originals and protected files, then check the result after confirming. Edited, open, pinned and uncertain files should remain protected. Exact Windows effects are still being checked. Do not remove a work-folder registration to bypass a refusal.

Inspect the current connection and pending local work. Open Settings > Storage to inspect usage and quota. Choose the available clear or storage-maintenance action. Review reclaimable files and protected files. Confirm only the reviewed changes and inspect the result. For relocation, use the supplied review and check the destination. Cache clear, Free up space and Discard Changes have different effects. Edited, open, pinned and uncertain files need protection. Cancel to keep the previous state. If clear or move fails, retain files and operation details; do not delete the cache manually. IMAGE PLACEHOLDER — Manage storage safely A Sambafied illustration will be added here. No application screenshot is available yet.

Ask your administrator to check the certificate chain and supported proxy route. Retain the error with private addresses redacted. Do not disable certificate validation or change trust settings as an improvised fix.

Check the connection, folder, query, filter and whether more results remain to load. Refresh and read the error. A filtered or denied asset is not necessarily deleted. Ask your administrator about permissions or expired-asset policy.

Keep the work folder’s Author and account visible as you move from editing to publication.

Recall the original before editing. Save through the desktop application as usual, then inspect the candidate’s Changes surface. A saved local file is not a receipt that AEM received the change. The inspected development code tracks root- and principal-bound generations in a journal. The Changes surface presents immutable generations rather than inferring a destination from a filename.

For a candidate that enables the bounded local on-premises publication adapter: Confirm the connection, work folder, and destination asset. Review the captured local generation and any pending or uncertain operation. Use the candidate’s explicit publication action. Confirm the resulting remote state before considering the operation complete. Manual publication is the default in the inspected local contract. A preference can opt in to future new-file uploads. It is not blanket approval to overwrite existing assets.

The local contract uses an explicit Create version & upload mine path for existing edits or name collisions. It verifies a recoverable remote version before replacement. That recovery mechanism is not an atomic multiwriter lock. The reviewed local Author accepts stale conditional binary updates; a preflight comparison cannot guarantee that another user will not write between the check and replacement. For an uncertain response, stop and reconcile the remote result before repeating the action. See conflicts and recovery.

The Explorer-action implementation includes check-out and check-in for an eligible registered asset. Check-in releases the current user’s checkout only and refuses unresolved local work, pending or unknown jobs, and open writers under its inspected contract. Check-in does not upload. Do not use it as a shortcut to publish edits.

These local adapters do not establish complete production sync or Cloud Service binary-write acceptance. Local deletion is not propagated to AEM under the inspected publication contract. Other operations—such as moving, deleting, duplicating, or bulk uploading repository content—need their own explicit qualification. Use readiness when planning a workflow.
Choose the right connection before you browse or search. A result belongs to an Author, account, and configured DAM scope; the same filename in another connection is a different asset.

Browse assets using the file window (Linux) or Explorer integration (Windows). The display shows a bounded page at a time. On Linux, use the file browser window to navigate the mounted FUSE filesystem: sambafied-desktop present On Windows, open the mapped drive letter in Explorer after connecting: sambafied-desktop status Use your configured evaluation subtree. A failed or partial listing does not establish that an asset was deleted.

The inspected desktop Search command has a bounded on-premises QueryBuilder adapter. Local checks cover a known asset, no-match results, rejected queries, and rejection after logout. They do not qualify every query, multi-page ordering, permission changes, or Cloud Service search. A search should retain its connection context. Clearing a search should not switch the selected connection or change authentication. Collections, advanced metadata discovery, and complete parity across deployment targets need their own acceptance. They are not implied by a successful single-asset search.

Navigate to the registered work folder in Explorer and open a known test original. If it is still cloud-only, the agent must obtain the original before the file can be used. Opening a file depends on its desktop application association and the candidate's actual handling of that file. This site does not publish a creative-application compatibility matrix. A linked document may depend on other files and their paths. Do not infer that opening one original also qualifies automatic dependency retrieval or relinking.

The inspected Explorer-action implementation includes Open in AEM and Copy AEM link for a registered asset. The URL points to the authorized AEM environment; it does not grant someone else access or make the asset public. Native menu activation and visual behavior have separate qualification requirements. See readiness and troubleshooting.

The core idea is familiar: navigate your AEM assets in a desktop folder and open a file where you work. The current native preview uses Windows Cloud Files integration, with bounded local AEM evidence.

A named connection identifies the Author and configured DAM subtree. A new, empty NTFS work folder is registered and populated from a bounded namespace snapshot. Files begin as cloud-only placeholders. Opening a supported original requests its bytes through the agent. The preview stages and verifies the original before completing recall. The original folder-preview slice documents a maximum of 1,000 entries and 16 levels. Treat these as preview constraints, not a production scale promise. Remote changes are not equivalent to a continuously refreshed mirror; evaluate the exact candidate’s refresh behavior.

A placeholder is not a complete local copy. A file that has already been fully recalled can remain accessible after the provider stops or the user logs out. A cloud-only file cannot be newly recalled without the required running, authenticated provider. This bounded behavior does not establish a complete offline mode. Do not rely on every asset being available without a connection, or interpret a status icon as an offline guarantee.

Saving locally and publishing to AEM are distinct events. Later local development work adds a durable change journal and explicit publication flows for configured local on-premises profiles. Manual publication is the default; existing edits and collisions have an explicit version-and-upload path. These are bounded local adapters, not a production sync guarantee. Check readiness for the distinction between implemented work and accepted deployment targets. The inspected local publication contract does not propagate a local file deletion to AEM. Do not delete or relocate pending work to clear a warning. Preserve local bytes and unresolved operations for diagnosis.

Stop disconnects active provider work while retaining the registration and working files. It is not a request to delete the folder. Unregister removes native registration after identity and lifecycle checks. Windows can remove cloud-only or partially recalled placeholders during unregister. The default command refuses those entries; an explicit discard option exists and can remove them. Fully resident originals and ordinary local-edited files are retained under the documented lifecycle contract. Before unregistering, inspect the exact root, preserve local changes, and use the candidate’s matching instructions. A retained or partially initialized folder must not be silently adopted as a fresh mount.

Check the exact candidate, AEM target, authentication profile, file type, and desktop application together. Background API checks do not establish Explorer appearance, navigation entries, keyboard access, or creative-app behavior.

The public product is coming soon. These instructions are for developers and evaluators who want to build Sambafied from source. A production installer and supported compatibility matrix are not yet available. Read readiness and limits before connecting. This guide describes evaluation preparation, not a production installation procedure.

Sambafied DAM Client is built in Rust and currently supports: Platform Status Notes Windows 10/11 (x64) Primary development target Requires Cloud Files API support (NTFS volume) Linux (x64) Supported Requires FUSE3, GTK4 and libadwaita for the file browser macOS Not yet qualified Linux and Windows are the current focus Build requirements: Rust toolchain (edition 2024) via rustup On Windows: Visual Studio Build Tools with C++ workload On Linux: FUSE3 development headers, GTK4, libadwaita

Clone the repository and build the desktop client: git clone https://github.com/sambafied/sambafied.git cd sambafied cargo build --release -p sambafied-desktop On Linux, to include the GTK file browser window: cargo build --release -p sambafied-desktop --features files-browser The binary is at target/release/sambafied-desktop (Linux) or target\release\sambafied-desktop.exe (Windows).

On Windows, use sambafied-desktop to map an SMB share: sambafied-desktop connect --drive S --share \\server\share --prompt sambafied-desktop status The --prompt flag opens the Windows credential dialog. To disconnect: sambafied-desktop disconnect --drive S The watch command runs the background agent for Explorer integration: sambafied-desktop watch

documents.t: The implemented desktop flow accepts an Author URL and opens the sign-in page. After a successful connection, the agent owns the session and work folder. Sign-in, mount, original recall, logout and remembered restore have bounded local evidence. A local sign-in result does not qualify your organization's SSO setup or an AEM as a Cloud Service session.

Open the work folder in Explorer (Windows) or the file browser (Linux). Navigate to a known test original and open it. Check the content against the known source. Record errors and status; an icon alone is not evidence that bytes transferred correctly. Do not use a local save as proof that a remote upload succeeded. Publication and sync have separate behavior and qualification boundaries.

On Windows, disconnect the mapped drive: sambafied-desktop disconnect --drive S On Linux, unmount the FUSE filesystem or stop the running mount process. Stopping and unregistering are different. Read the folder lifecycle before removing a registration. Preserve any local edits and uncertain publication state for review. If a step fails, use troubleshooting. Avoid repeatedly creating replacement roots or deleting retained state.

Give each connection a recognizable name and record its intended Author and DAM subtree. Use a distinct, empty work-folder path for each new mapping. Confirm the signed-in identity and target before performing any operation. Evaluate each target and authentication profile independently. The complete experience needs evidence for simultaneous connections, independent sign-in and logout, restore after restart, destination clarity, publication routing, and failure isolation. Sambafied DAM Client is being built around a native desktop folder experience: navigate assets through familiar filesystem paths and keep separate AEM instances in separate working folders. The intended experience is similar in spirit to OneDrive’s folder workflow. This is a workflow analogy, not a claim of feature parity or a Microsoft integration.

Creative work often involves opening, placing, and navigating files across several desktop tools. A folder-first workflow aims to keep those files within the places people already use, rather than requiring a separate asset browser for every interaction. The current Windows preview has exercised a bounded AEM namespace in Explorer and on-demand recall of originals. The desktop window and tray provide connection and status surfaces; the filesystem is central to the intended everyday experience.

The connection model includes named profiles and explicit mount paths. The goal is to use one client for multiple AEM instances, each mapped to its own folder. Full concurrent multi-instance operation is still subject to qualification. See multiple instances for a concrete mapping example and the separation rules to consider.

Both deployment paths are in product scope. Use the local AEM connection guide or Cloud Service connection guide. Authentication and operation acceptance remain specific to each environment; a local result does not certify every Cloud or production configuration.
